text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a latency regression on the v2 model canary for /generate. p50 is +12ms, p95 is +45ms vs control over the last 30m :eyes:. Not correlated with traffic bump. Anyone see this in the kernel/batching dashboards?

alex: I shipped a small kernel-selector tweak ~1h ago to prefer fused-matmul for batch shapes with >64 tokens. It was supposed to win for long context but maybe it flipped for our common short-chat traces. rolling it back now to verify. :gear:

jun: Profiling (short run) shows an increase in memcpy and auth-queue wait. KV cache hit rate dropped from 87% -> 74% for that route on the canary hosts. Looks like the selection caused a different memory layout and evictions. snippet from perf: 
```
flame: kernel_execute -> memcpy 18ms -> kv_lookup 6ms -> attention_kernel 9ms
control: kernel_execute -> memcpy 6ms -> kv_lookup 2ms -> attention_kernel 10ms
```

priya: Interesting — also seeing more small batches (batchsize=1) being packed into the continuous-kernel path which expects larger batchshapes. That could increase overhead per token. Suggest we: 1) rollback selector (alex), 2) enable prefix-KV sticky routing for canary, 3) run a micro-benchmark splitting by route and model-version.

alex: Rollback done, canary traffic now on the previous kernel rule. Deploy-bot shows: 
`deploy-bot: canary-v2-kernel-selector -> rolled back by alex at 1717004387`

maria: After rollback metrics trending back towards control, p95 delta down to +8ms, kv-hit up ~6%. Good catch. Can we add a per-route token-level waterfall panel that attributes time to memcpy / kv_lookup / kernel so we can catch this earlier? :chart_with_upwards_trend:

jun: I'll add a lightweight instrument that emits token-sli split tags and a small Grafana panel (sparkline + stacked bar). Will also add a tiny sampling profiler on canary hosts for the next 2 hours.

priya: Also file an eval: run the standard prompt set across v1/v2 with multiple batchshapes to surface these layout regressions automatically. tagging @sre for infra noise.

maria: Thanks — let's reconvene if the profiler shows anything else. short thread but useful. :thumbsup:
